conventions: yamin → 'right hand' (vv.1, 5) is one unit headed on 'right': the ASV never writes bare 'hand' for this noun, so 'hand' is the supplied generic under rule 31's tie-break and 'right' carries the lexeme. Heading on 'hand' is the named alternative in both notes.
report: Checked all seven candidate lemmas. Every difference is one the ASV's English licenses: the suffix takes 'thy' or 'thine' as written (vv.1-3) and goes unrepresented only in the lexicalized Adonai title (v.5, rule 57), while the 'my' of v.1 is on the common noun adon with a written possessive; be- takes 'among' (v.6) or 'in' (vv.2,3,5,7) as written; min takes 'out of' (vv.2,3) or the partitive 'of' (v.7); 'al takes 'After', 'at', 'in' as written; 'enemies' is a bare object in v.1 and a rectum with 'of' in v.2; machats carries 'He' in v.6 and not in v.5, where 'The Lord' is the written subject.

Recurring analyses agree across verses: yamin → 'right hand' heads on 'right' in v.1 and v.5; construct nouns take the supplied 'the' and recta the 'of' in vv.2,3,5; the assimilated article takes the written 'the' in vv.6,7; machats keeps 'through' with the verb in vv.5,6 as rum keeps 'up' in v.7.

The one large-source unit (v.1 hadom + le + raglei → 'footstool') stands: the single English word writes both lexemes and carries the lamed, so rule 30 fuses it as rule 23 fuses 'horsehoofs', and rule 22 forbids leaving regel unrepresented beside a word that spells it. The v.6 supplied object 'the places' is correctly added and 'with' correctly the verb's (rule 44).
The single BSB disagreement (v.5 Adonai suffix) is the documented rule 57 convention, not an error.
No rule learned; the chapter applies existing rules only.
